author: James Grant
title: Longview football leaning on culture to make another run at state in 2025 - NewsBreak
text: LONGVIEW, Texas ( KETK ) – Longview quarterback Tre Hamilton hasn’t forgotten the feeling of losing to Southlake Carroll on a last-second field goal in the 6A-D2 state semifinals last year. “I’ve seen all those seniors cry. I ain’t want that to happen for these upcoming seniors this year, so I plan on winning that game this year,” Hamilton said. Hamilton worked hard this offseason and is poised to lead the Lobos back to state to finish the job this season. “Fixing some of my mechanics and getting bigger, stronger, and faster like usual. Also, just making sure I do what I need to do as a leader for this team,” Hamilton said. Hamilton, who was thrust into the starting role as a sophomore during last year’s playoffs, made the most of his opportunity and gained experience along the way. “It was very valuable to me. I had a lot of fun out there throwing touchdowns and having the Lobo fans out there cheering us on,” Hamilton said. While the Lobos lost record-breaking running back Kelvin “Boosie” Washington, who’s now at Tulsa, they return weapons on offense, including sophomore wideout Jaden Hurndon. “Probably the best receiver in our receiver room. You can also tell from whenever you see ’em on the field. Also, just him out there running routes. Every time you throw it to ’em it’s pretty much a touchdown,” Hamilton said. Longview lost four out of five starters on the offensive line, and three all-state linebackers, but senior cornerback Da’Kayden Carter said the Lobos’ defense has potential if they do the little things right. “We’re gonna have to tackle this year. We’re gonna have to tackle. We gotta play together again,” Carter said. Longview head football coach John King, who’s led Longview to 234 wins and one state title in his 21 seasons at the helm, said the Lobos’ culture should pave the way for more success this season. “Our mindset’s always been to develop a program where you can sustain it from year to year. You know, we’re not going to coach a good team; we have a good team. We hope we have a good program where kids build and develop each year, and when it’s their time to shine, they’re in a position where they can,” King said. While there may be questions at different spots on the field, the expectations in Longview remain the same. “It’s Lobo Football. The expectations are always high. We’ll see if they can live up to the expectations. We plan to be playing football in the playoffs,” King said. The Lobos welcome longtime East Texas rival Lufkin to town in Week One. Kickoff is set for 7:30 p.m. at Lobo Stadium in Longview, Friday, August 29. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to KETK.com | FOX51.com.
